about: Each certificate says: in the term model `model`, which satisfies the model's law (z3-only, term_models_z3.py), the target law fails at the elements `at`; so the model's law does not imply the target law (over all structures, infinite ones included). `lhs` and `rhs` are the two sides' values there. `not_refuted` lists targets for which no failure was found; `z3` is z3's answer to 'does the target fail somewhere in the model' (unsat = it holds on all terms, z3-only).
elements: constructor terms: G, F(t), P(a,b); different terms are different elements

A.definition: x*y = P(x,y);  f(t) = b if t = P(x,P(b,z)), else t

B.definition: f(t) = F(t);  x*w = b if w = P(b,F(z)), else P(x,w)

C.definition: f(t) = F(t);  u*z = b if u = P(F(t),b), else P(u,z)

D.definition: x*y = P(x,y);  f(t) = b if t = P(P(a,b),z), else t
